intent.subject: Corporal Mahmoud (C-04), radio operator.
intent.action: His thumb hovers over the field radio switch as he uneasily whispers that command will not know their position, warning Shalabi without defiance.
intent.setting: Tina Plain marsh at night, with the manpack radio close at hand.
intent.mood: Tense, hushed, and apprehensive; red-filtered light leaves his three-quarter face readable against the darkness.

research.claim: The company is shown beginning its march through the Tina Plain/marsh after the early helicopter drop.
research.note: Follows production decision D-1 to use the Egyptian account of the early Tina Plain drop and long march; the landing location and march distance remain disputed and require the episode end-card source note.

research.claim: The precise setting of this first-march moment as full night is not explicitly established in the ledger.
research.note: H-05 and H-08 support the drop and march, but do not establish this beat's exact time of night.

research.claim: Composite Corporal Mahmoud sends/receives and decodes the coded radio traffic, warns Shalabi that the signal was intercepted, worries about losing contact with command, and switches off the set.
research.note: Mahmoud is a composite character. His actions dramatize the sourced intercepted-signal and radio-silence event without assigning it to a documented real individual.

research.claim: Captain Hamdi Shalabi orders radio silence after the intercepted-signal warning.
research.note: The coded warning and Shalabi's radio-silence order are stated by the primary Egyptian account; the marked dialogue is a permitted dramatized paraphrase.

research.claim: Shalabi taps the switched-off radio and draws a finger across his lips to communicate the sourced radio-silence order; the file passes the silent signal back man to man.
research.note: Permitted staging under P-01: the gestures visually show the sourced radio-silence order and add no new event or outcome.

research.claim: Composite Sergeant Sayed hears the silence order and asks whether the enemy is waiting for them.
research.note: Sayed is a composite character; the question is fictional character dialogue and does not credit him with a documented act.

research.claim: Shalabi uses his compass, changes the file's bearing, and directs the company toward an unexpected approach after the interception warning.
research.note: The route-change dialogue is an approved paraphrase of the source treatment that the enemy did not expect anyone to come from that direction. The compass and turning-file business are permitted P-01 staging.

research.claim: The Soviet-pattern manpack radio, whip antenna, handset placement, and use of red light are presented as period equipment/detail.
research.note: The ledger documents radio traffic and silence, but does not source this specific radio model/configuration or red-light procedure.

flags.detail: The beat fixes the company's first steps into the marsh at night, but the ledger does not establish the exact time for this moment.
The specific Soviet-pattern manpack radio configuration, whip antenna, handset placement, and red-light decoding procedure are not sourced in the ledger.

direction.coverage: Begin in a tight three-quarter close-up, then cut to Mahmoud’s hovering thumb and radio switch before returning to his wary glance toward Shalabi.
direction.blocking: Mahmoud crouches beside the manpack radio, body angled protectively over it, thumb suspended above the switch as he turns only his eyes toward Shalabi.
direction.performance_note: Whisper the warning with controlled fear and professional restraint, seeking confirmation rather than challenging command.
direction.pacing: Hold the silence and hesitation before the line, then let the gesture remain unresolved for a beat afterward.
direction.tone_ref: Restrained historical war realism: red-filtered practical light, marsh darkness, and quiet dread over overt drama.

wardrobe.additions: short military haircut, backpack field radio with a whip antenna (PRP-0007); wire-rimmed glasses taped at the hinge
visible_details: Bare-headed short black hair; wire-rimmed glasses with a small taped hinge clearly readable in the red-filtered light.
Sand-khaki 1973 cotton field jacket at chest-and-shoulder level, with two buttoned chest-pocket flaps and sleeves rolled to the forearms.
Plain khaki collar: no red collar tabs, chest eagle badge, rank stars, or modern insignia.
Soviet-pattern khaki canvas chest-rig straps and one or more closed-flap magazine pouches at the lower edge of frame; plain cotton webbing and simple metal buckle only.
Backpack field radio PRP-0007 immediately beside/against him, with its period canvas harness and whip antenna partly entering frame; his hovering thumb is at the radio switch.
WEAR_MUD reads as dark wet mud-and-brine splashes across the jacket front, cuffs, straps, and pouch flaps, with damp fabric sheen and a few pale salt traces; no blood or damage.
wardrobe.notes: MCU prioritizes Mahmoud’s taped glasses, plain collar, period canvas webbing, and wet marsh wear; soaked trousers above the knees and boots remain off-frame but retain locked continuity. This is a new angle after Shalabi’s close-up: preserve the same cold marsh humidity and night moisture, while Mahmoud alone receives the restrained red radio-light effect.

makeup.skin_state: Light wheat-colored skin is damp with cold marsh exertion, with a restrained wet sheen on forehead, nose, cheekbones and upper lip. Fine dark mud flecks and thin brine streaks mark the lower cheeks, jawline and neck; a few pale salt traces catch in his sparse light-brown eyebrows and curled mustache. Freckles across nose and cheeks remain visible beneath the grime; no blood or visible wounds.
makeup.hair_state: Bare-headed thick wavy light-brown hair is humidity-damp, tousled and slightly flattened at the temples, with a few wet strands separated over the forehead. Preserve the curled mustache and its upturned ends, damp but intact; light green-grey eyes are tired, alert and reflect the dim red-filtered practical without appearing brightly lit.
makeup.notes: Professional fatigue and controlled apprehension only; keep the three-quarter face readable in the red-filtered flashlight and minimal cold starlight, with darkness holding the far side of the face.

dressing: Thin fractured white salt crust over black mud
Shallow mid-shin brine sheets with small cold sky reflections
Sparse low salt-marsh scrub, dark and wind-flattened
A small red-filtered flashlight propped beside the radio, its covered beam directed upward without revealing any text or controls
set.set_state: Mahmoud crouches in the cold, featureless night marsh, keeping the mud-smeared PRP-0007 raised clear of the mid-shin brine on a firmer salt-crust patch as his thumb hovers over its switch.
set.notes: Keep the radio, its controls, and Mahmoud's hovering thumb in the lower foreground while the red practical and faint starlight make his three-quarter face readable; no other person or equipment enters frame.

camera.light: A tightly flagged, dim red-filtered flashlight practical rises from beside the radio, grazing Mahmoud’s near cheek, mouth, taped-hinge glasses, hovering thumb and switch; faint cool starlight/moonlight supplies a blue-black edge on his hair and shoulder, with the marsh falling rapidly to near-black. Keep the red practical localized and motivated by its covered upward beam, with no broad artificial fill.
camera.exposure_note: Expose low for a genuinely dark night exterior while retaining readable detail in Mahmoud’s light wheat-colored complexion: preserve subdued warm-red modeling on the face and mouth, restrained cool separation in the shadows, and no clipped flashlight hotspot or brightly illuminated background. Hold the radio switch and hovering thumb about a stop below the face so the gesture remains visible but tense.
camera.framing_note: Generate 16:9 with Mahmoud’s three-quarter face, both eyes, clearly readable lip-sync mouth, glasses, hovering thumb, radio switch, and small red practical all inside the central middle 75% height for the 2.39:1 crop. Keep his eyeline angled toward off-screen Shalabi and use shallow 85mm falloff to leave salt crust and dark brine soft behind him.

action.choreography: Mahmoud stays in a low, stable crouch beside the manpack radio, torso angled protectively over it; he speaks in a controlled whisper without committing to the switch. His hovering hand remains visibly tense but measured, with no abrupt movement that would disturb the radio or splash the shallow brine.
action.movement: Minimal crouched weight shift in mid-shin marsh mud; only his eyes turn toward off-screen Shalabi while his thumb holds above the radio switch.
beats: Hold a quiet crouch over PRP-0007, one hand steadying his balance near the set.
Raise his thumb to hover just above the radio switch without touching it.
Whisper the warning, mouth clearly visible in three-quarter view.
Shift only his eyes toward off-screen Shalabi, keeping his body and radio covered.
Hold the unresolved hover for a final beat.
action.safety_note: Keep his planted boots and crouch stable in shallow mid-shin brine and mud; avoid a sudden weight transfer or visible splash near the radio.

reasons: The intent identifies the subject, decisive action, Tina Plain marsh setting, night time of day, and a tense, hushed mood.
It preserves the scripted dramatic beat: Mahmoud hesitates over the shutoff while voicing the consequence of radio silence to Shalabi.
It references the available character and location library IDs (C-04 and LOC-0003) and identifies the relevant radio and red-light elements without requiring IDs for the warning or order.
No invented historical event or unsupported factual claim is introduced; the phrasing remains a faithful dramatic rendering of the locked beat.

Coverage is specific and motivated: a tight three-quarter close-up establishes Mahmoud’s apprehension, an insert isolates the consequential hovering thumb/radio switch, and the return glance preserves the warning’s relationship to Shalabi.
Blocking places Mahmoud crouched beside and protectively over the manpack radio, with the suspended thumb and eye-only turn clearly supporting secrecy, tension, and the intended restrained posture.
The performance note directs controlled fear, professional restraint, and non-defiant intent, matching Mahmoud’s uneasy warning without making him confrontational.
Pacing explicitly preserves silence, hesitation, and an unresolved aftermath, appropriate to the tense, hushed nighttime scene.
The tone reference is consistent with grounded historical war drama and the specified red-filtered light, marsh darkness, and quiet apprehension.

C-04 is correctly bare-headed in mud-worn, period-appropriate Egyptian field uniform and Soviet-pattern webbing, with plain khaki collar and no forbidden collar tabs, chest eagle, or invented insignia.

The locked radio PRP-0007 is retained and described consistently with Mahmoud's protective crouch; the wardrobe wear state is compatible with the shallow salt-marsh environment and prior damp/mud continuity.

Mahmoud's hair continuity conflicts with the previous-shot specification: it was established as short black military-cut hair, but this output changes it to medium-length wavy light-brown hair with tousled strands. Medium-length hair also conflicts with the production requirement for Egyptian commandos to have short black hair.
The revised hair description risks breaking recognition continuity despite retaining the curled mustache and damp, mud-flecked condition.
revise_instructions: Replace the medium-length wavy light-brown hair description with Mahmoud's established short black military-cut hair, damp and flattened at the temple and hairline. Retain the curled mustache, light stubble, light-wheat damp skin, restrained brine sheen, mud flecks, and uninjured condition.

reasons: The red-filtered flashlight is required to motivate the red practical illumination, but Set specifies only a red glow and does not physically place or identify the flashlight source. This leaves the camera lighting without a defined on-set motivation.
PRP-0007 and the shallow-water rule are otherwise handled correctly: the radio is a hand prop and is kept above mud and standing water.
revise_instructions: Specify the physical placement of the red-filtered flashlight practical—for example, secured immediately beside the radio controls or held just off-frame by Mahmoud—so it can cast the tight red pool on his face, thumb, and switch without adding red spill into the marsh. Keep it period-plausible and ensure it does not displace or obscure PRP-0007.

reasons: The static MCU, 85 mm portrait lens, night looks, 16:9 generation with 2.39:1 crop-safe framing, and readable lip-sync mouth all match the locked shot design.

The exposure and lighting plan preserves a dark night image while keeping Mahmoud's eye, mouth, hovering thumb, and radio switch readable; it also maintains the intended red practical/cool moonlight separation.
The choreography directly serves the beat: Mahmoud remains crouched, whispers with controlled professional unease, looks only toward Shalabi, and leaves the switch action unresolved.
It respects the shallow marsh constraint and keeps the radio close, still, and out of the water/mud as established by Set. No unsupported combat event or inappropriate weapon action is introduced.

The instruction to keep the radio pack “planted close beside his knee” is ambiguous in a shallow brine marsh and can imply that the locked carried radio is resting in mud or water. This conflicts with the production rule that weapons and loads must be carried clear of water and mud.
revise_instructions: Specify that Mahmoud supports or braces PRP-0007 above the brine and mud beside his knee while operating it, rather than planting it on the marsh surface. Retain the static crouch, hovering thumb, and unresolved transmission.

reasons: The visible-details entry says Mahmoud's trousers are soaked with mud and brine above the knees. The locked location rule limits standing marsh water to mid-shin, with only occasional knee-depth pockets, and explicitly prohibits water above the knee unless a man has fallen or is kneeling; Mahmoud is described as crouching, not kneeling.
revise_instructions: Revise the lower-trouser wear to wet mud/brine staining through the mid-shin area and, at most, around the knees if justified by the crouch. Do not specify soaking or water exposure above the knees.

reasons: The exposure note specifies Mahmoud as having “medium-olive skin,” while the makeup department establishes his skin as light wheat-colored. This creates an avoidable cross-department continuity conflict for the facial exposure and color rendering of a lip-sync close shot.
revise_instructions: Revise the exposure note to preserve Mahmoud’s established light wheat-colored complexion under the restrained red practical and cool starlight, rather than specifying medium-olive skin.

reasons: Matches the locked MCU, 85mm portrait lens, static move, night looks, and 16:9 generation/2.39:1 delivery requirements.
Exposure guidance keeps the exterior genuinely dark while preserving Mahmoud's three-quarter face, mouth, thumb, and radio switch for lip-sync and key action.
Central crop-safe framing keeps the required face and gesture readable, with an off-screen eyeline toward Shalabi.

department_notes: set: The Director's requested cutaway and return conflict with the locked static 5-second shot; retain one static composition that contains both Mahmoud's face and the radio switch.

action: The Director’s requested cutaway to Mahmoud’s thumb and return glance conflicts with the locked static MCU shot, so the thumb, switch, and wary eye-line must be held within the single locked composition.

critic: Director coverage calls for a tight close-up followed by a cut to the thumb/radio switch and a return glance, which conflicts with the locked single MCU/static shot design. The departments correctly follow the lock; production should resolve the coverage request at the shot-design level rather than require these departments to add cuts.

issues: [design_match/major] [L-0002] Mahmoud is gripping a handheld radio with both hands rather than holding his thumb visibly hovering over the field-radio switch, so the opening action cue is not readable.
[period_accuracy/major] [L-0003] The compact handheld black radio and conspicuous glowing red control do not convincingly match the specified 1973 Egyptian backpack field radio.
[lighting/major] The named red-filtered flashlight does not light Mahmoud's face; almost all red illumination is isolated to the radio control and fingers.
[anatomy_proportions/major] [L-0013] Mahmoud's shoulders are approximately 2.1 head widths across, so his head appears too large for his slight but adult frame.

[props_weapons/major] [L-0003] The visible black radio/control box has modern-looking modular connectors and detailing inconsistent with an identifiable 1973 Soviet-pattern Egyptian backpack field radio.
[design_match/major] [L-0002] The scripted action cue is wrong or ambiguous: the index finger appears extended against the controls rather than Mahmoud's thumb visibly hovering over the switch.

[lighting/major] The designed red-filtered, starlit night look is absent: strong neutral frontal illumination makes Mahmoud and the marsh substantially too bright, and almost no red light reaches his face or hand.
